github_release_policy: During development, only externally acquired immutable source payloads and source-acquisition packs such as PDF, HTML, filings and formal announcement bytes belong in the shared GitHub Release. Actions may download them directly from the external web, hash them, upload uniquely named immutable Release assets, and later restore only the source pack required by the current task. Release transport never changes source authority.
google_drive_policy: Longcycle-generated binary state belongs in Google Drive: DuckDB replay materializations, execution/reconciliation outputs, generated database snapshots and offline runtimes. Do not put externally acquired original PDF/HTML/source bytes in Drive by default. Drive is a portable generated-state relay, not the live transactional database authority.
postgres_policy: Do not transport a live PostgreSQL cluster as session state or place it in GitHub Release. PostgreSQL remains the transactional write/ops engine and is rebuilt in a service-capable runtime when writes, leases or outbox semantics are required. If a generated database snapshot is ever needed for handoff, it belongs in Google Drive and remains a snapshot rather than live authority.
duckdb_policy: DuckDB is the portable read/replay materialization. Restore a required generated capsule from Google Drive, verify recorded SHA-256 values, and open research packs read-only. Raw source bytes required for re-grounding are restored separately from GitHub Release.
supersession_policy: Both transports are immutable-by-identity for handoff purposes. Never replace bytes behind a recorded source Release filename or a recorded generated-state file id without advancing the repository manifest and SHA-256. Successor source packs get new Release filenames; successor generated packs get new Drive files/ids. This manifest is deliberately resume-relevant rather than an exhaustive historical asset inventory; durable receipts retain older artifact identities.
